A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DitHub framework and benchmarks. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DitHub evaluations on ODinW-13 and ODinW-O, component ablations, specialization experiments and unlearning results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds longitudinal and per-task forgetting results.

M1.justification: Warmup, class-specific A matrices, shared B updates, fetch/merge operations and averaged-module inference remain unchanged. The rewritten inference description clarifies the existing procedure without establishing an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ODinW-13 tasks, six-task ODinW-O construction, COCO evaluation and few-shot scenarios. The forgetting analyses and expanded domain illustrations use existing coverage.

E2.justification: External baseline membership and the EnE comparison remain unchanged. However, the component comparison drops the standalone shared-B-merging variant labeled '+Eq. 4' in v1 Figure 7; this comparator is absent from v2 Figure 8.

E3.justification: v2 adds normalized retention relative to initial task performance and final-minus-initial mAP forgetting metrics in Figure 4 and Appendix B. Existing benchmark settings and training hyperparameters remain unchanged; these additions do not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands direct analysis of forgetting through task-sequence retention curves and per-task forgetting tables for both benchmarks. It also removes the isolated B-merging-without-warmup ablation, while retaining the other component, sensitivity, specialization and unlearning analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three-seed averaging and identical standard-deviation tables. v2 specifically clarifies that task order depends on the selected seed, whereas v1 only mentions random shuffling. No increased run count or additional uncertainty estimates for the forgetting analyses are reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial temporal and taskwise forgetting results: Tables C/D report DitHub versus ZiRa average changes of -1.73 versus -6.66 mAP on ODinW-13 and -2.68 versus -3.84 on ODinW-O. Existing benchmark scores remain unchanged. The 55.91 B-only ablation result disappears, and the stated aggregate ablation gain is corrected from 6.22 to 6.13.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 drops the 'disjoint tasks' input qualifier, aligning its specification with the overlapping-class setting already described in Section 3. Otherwise, the mathematical content is equivalent: the LoRA identity moves inline, merge equations are renumbered, and no proofs are added.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly adds separating warmup from specialization to its contribution list and foregrounds the existing 4.21 mAP margin in the introduction. Table 1 identifies this as the margin over ZiRa. The central modularity, composition-novelty and benchmark-performance claims retain their scope.

C2.justification: New interpretations distinguish forgetting in shared B and class-specific A, explain positive transfer on Packages, and acknowledge difficulty retaining aerial-domain knowledge. Appendix F adds concrete limitations concerning empirical merge coefficients and missing explicit domain information. Appendix D.2 also adds a co-occurrence explanation for the unchanged unlearning matrix.

D1.justification: v2 supplies task-order listings for the forgetting analyses and explicitly states that merged-module inference uses one forward pass. It removes v1's project-page URL. Hardware, model configuration, LoRA rank, optimizer settings and resource figures remain the same.

R1.justification: Five references are added: works on forgetting by Boschini and Chaudhry, MDETR, AdamW, and Mancusi's tracking-specialization study. These provide limited additional grounding; the related-work narrative and claimed positioning of DitHub remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Extensive sentence and paragraph revisions condense the method and experimental discussion. Former Sections 5.2 and 5.3 are merged, and the appendices are reorganized with a separate outline and relocated implementation details. This constitutes substantial editorial restructuring beyond the scientific additions.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout, extensively repositioning figures, tables and captions. Figure 1 is rearranged into training/inference panels, new forgetting displays are added, Figure B expands from two illustrated classes to five, and the component-ablation chart loses one bar.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides more direct evidence for its anti-forgetting claims and states concrete limitations of its merging strategy, improving assessment of the unchanged method. It also corrects the ablation-gain arithmetic. These gains outweigh the loss of one diagnostic ablation and the project-page link, yielding a limited overall improvement.
